quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible. Use turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid sudden hazards.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride in the far right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you leave the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you leave the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a blind spot, either speed up or slow down to leave it.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Happen because passengers distract riders.
Occur at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a new motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do these actions separately—not at the same time. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms are straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the grips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Means that they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not consciously see them.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At high speeds.
After riding for a long time.
Far from home.
On short trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly apply it again.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not notice them.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works properly.
Assume you know where all controls are located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be driving slowly looking for parking.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create several dangers. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place loads low. Placing them high, like on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Spread the load evenly on both sides to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press down the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is following too closely before you slow down. The driver may not notice an upcoming hazard. Also flash it if you are slowing in an unexpected place.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare it away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting something small is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery surfaces.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use when used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use when used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.
It fits snugly.
It is free of defects.
It has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet must be DOT certified and fit snugly to protect you. It should have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can pass dangers more quickly.
You have a narrow view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can follow the next vehicle more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view, more time to react to hazards, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left
The center
The right
It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding away from them may make them re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: The best lane position is one that:

options.text: Lets you travel the fastest.
Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Allows other drivers to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that maximizes your space cushion.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes firmly at the same time to stop quickly. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Piling loads on the back raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Accelerate before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only one brake for non-emergencies.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and lets you be seen.
Increases your space cushion and lets you be seen.
Increases road hazards and lets others pass you.
Reduces road hazards and lets you follow vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and lets you be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that maximizes your space cushion.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Stop them any way you can. Recruit other friends to apply peer pressure and prevent them from riding.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT need to be checked regularly?

options.text: The brakes
The fasteners
The tires
The paint

questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Even small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous while riding.

questions.question: To swerve correctly on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve safely, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right grip to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left grip.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain behind other vehicles?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions. Increase this distance when weather is bad or conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn
Flash your lights
Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it
Move to another lane if necessary

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if necessary
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging onto the highway. Move to a lane farther from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly
Steer in a weaving pattern to match the grooves
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight ahead
Move to the left side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight ahead
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Just stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not try to zigzag to match the weave—this makes it worse.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the vehicle ahead too closely
Someone is sitting in a parked car
You want people to notice your motorcycle
You are passing someone in the street

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others before passing them. If a driver next to you is following too closely, they may cut in front of you. If someone is in a parked car or walking in the street, sound your horn as you pass. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: Several factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT play a role?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast someone drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration is affected by how much alcohol someone drinks, how quickly they drink it, and their body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front wheel
Look through the turn toward where you want to go
Turn your entire body to see through the turn
Speed up before the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn toward where you want to go
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to:

options.text: Watch for parked cars entering traffic
Look for vehicles changing lanes
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down
See if someone is turning behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors at a stop to check for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are very close. You may need to react quickly to stay safe.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is usually the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off the road and wait for the rain to stop
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead
Increase your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this can change depending on traffic.
